title: Deeper/broader PAR-139 XCLIP adapter loss and semantic boundary
mode: Primary-source documentation review, current downstream issue screen, and local read/callback/storage/writer audit
head: de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
scope: Check the recent XCLIP/SPATIAL_FILTER consumer report against primary DXF/AutoCAD API documentation.
Trace DWG and DXF SPATIAL_FILTER callbacks through the in-tree dwg2dxf adapter and identify existing low-level parser/writer support.
Compare available open-source DXF clipping APIs and explicitly separate object preservation from clipping/render semantics.
Add an implementation-ready PAR-139 leaf under existing PAR-06 without increasing the top-level subplan count or recurring validation cost.

sources.name: CADCraft downstream report
sources.observed: Issue opened 2026-10-18 against CADCraft 0.8.0 / AutoCAD 2027: the reporter says an XREF drawing clipped in AutoCAD displays unclipped in CADCraft. No sample drawing is attached. The report also mentions 6031 zero-length-line audit repairs; the issue bot explicitly separates these symptoms. SPATIAL_FILTER is presented as a possible cause, not a confirmed diagnosis.

sources.name: Autodesk SPATIAL_FILTER and DICTIONARY DXF references
sources.observed: The SPATIAL_FILTER schema defines point count, repeated OCS boundary coordinates, normal/origin, display and front/back clip flags/distances, and two repeated 12-value 4x3 transforms. The object owner is a SPATIAL dictionary. DICTIONARY entries are ordered/repeated name and handle pairs; common object fields distinguish owner-dictionary and extension-dictionary references.

sources.name: Autodesk AutoCAD .NET clipping API and developer example
sources.observed: The documented association path attaches the filter through the block reference extension dictionary, a child dictionary named ACAD_FILTER, and its SPATIAL entry. This makes the owner closure part of preservation correctness, not an optional rendering detail.

sources.name: ezdxf XClip and rendering/disassembly disclosures
sources.observed: The current documentation identifies ezdxf 1.4.5's 2D XClip helper, access to the underlying SPATIAL_FILTER and supported clipped-block rendering. It explicitly says the XClip helper cannot create inverted paths and INSERT disassembly does not apply XCLIP. Therefore disassembly output is not a clipping/render oracle; ezdxf is at most an optional pinned DXF-side comparator for the exact supported 2D profile.

localEvidence: src/intern/dwgreader.cpp:12960-12965 dispatches parsed SPATIAL_FILTER through DRW_Interface::addSpatialFilter.
src/drw_interface.h:549-550 provides a non-pure default no-op addSpatialFilter callback.
src/libdxfrw.cpp:17955-17960 routes DXF SPATIAL_FILTER through processRawCapturedObject, which invokes both the typed callback and addRawDxfObject.
dwg2dxf/dx_iface.h and dwg2dxf/dx_data.h contain no SPATIAL_FILTER callback override or typed collection; dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp:7012 onward has no SPATIAL_FILTER raw-retention branch.

src/libdxfrw.cpp:23201 and src/libdwgr.cpp:3340 expose low-level SPATIAL_FILTER output entry points, so the confirmed gap is the concrete adapter/object-graph route rather than absence of all serializers.

assessment.planImpact: PAR-139 records the confirmed in-tree adapter loss for SPATIAL_FILTER on DWG-origin and DXF-origin conversion. Its implementation sequence covers bounded typed/raw capture, order-independent INSERT-to-extension-dictionary owner closure, role-aware remapping, transactional refusal, and generated ASCII/Binary fast controls. Object preservation is distinct from clipping behavior; ezdxf's optional 2D comparison is route-limited, disassembly is explicitly non-clipping, and CADCraft issue #1581 remains a no-sample downstream hypothesis with separate audit symptoms. Existing fast validation cadence and external-J dispositions are unchanged.

method.kind: Read-only primary documentation / current issue review and local source trace; plan and receipt update only
method.limitations: The CADCraft issue provides no drawing and only hypothesizes a clipping cause. No external consumer result or visual semantics were independently reproduced. Autodesk's documented graph and the local missing adapter retention are sufficient to confirm a local serialization-path omission, not to identify the cause of CADCraft's observed output. The optional ezdxf comparator was source-reviewed, not run; its supported 2D profile does not qualify inverted/depth/tilted clipping or native CAD behavior.
